use_case: Predictive maintenance model for well equipment: predicts rod pump and ESP failures up to 30 days ahead from historian replica and work order data to prioritize workover rigs and pulling units
business_owner: Vice President, Operations Technology and Automation (with the Vice President, Permian Operations as main user)
vendor_or_model: Company-owned gradient-boosted classification models on the Cloud B machine learning platform
data_categories: SCADA historian replica data (pump cards, motor current, runtime, pressures, rates); ERP work order history with technician names removed; no personal information
consequential_decision_category: None (equipment); escalates to Safety/CI if outputs ever drive equipment or defer safety-critical inspections, and to Employment if used to evaluate crews
human_in_the_loop: A production engineer reviews every alert and decides whether to raise a work order; no write path to SCADA or the ERP
applicable_laws: No sector AI rule; FTC Act Section 5 for claims the company makes about the model; Texas TRAIGA intent-based prohibitions (none engaged)
status: In production (about 5,200 wells: Permian 3,900 after the 2026-05 expansion; legacy Mid-Continent 1,300); AQ-MC and Florida excluded
bias_or_representativeness_testing: Well group review done before the expansion; not repeated after it (POAM-020); cellular-polled ESP group flagged in section 7
monitoring: Monthly recall and precision; quarterly well group report; drift check on data changes
